next_unit_hint: The null is mechanistically expected and now measured: the protocol submits each document once, so a segmented/frequency policy has no re-access to promote anything on and slru degenerates to lru on a scan. Any further eviction work must change the WORKLOAD, not the flag: e.g. a hot set of ~10 documents re-requested every K insertions with total pressure > capacity (that is the only shape where slru's protected segment can hold anything), or M4's 8-request boundary probe repeated under slru to see whether the 30-31 document window moves. Separately, token_capacity is re-profiled at every start and fell 1620892 -> 1480094 (variant) -> 1440049 (restored production) across two restarts with no flag changed; a capacity-sensitive comparison needs the pool pinned (e.g. --max-total-tokens), not merely re-read.

assumptions.stop_surface: MEASURED AGAIN: gx10-occamy-nvfp4 carries HostConfig.AutoRemove=true and is the ExecStart of the systemd USER unit gx10-occamy-nvfp4.service (Restart=on-failure), so `docker stop` deletes the container and `docker start` would have nothing to start. The card's stop/start pair is therefore executed one level up: `systemctl --user stop` / `systemctl --user start`. The production container was never `rm`-ed by this unit (docker events: die+destroy at 07:46:24Z caused by the unit stop, then create+start wt-slru only).
assumptions.capacity_not_a_config_key: max_total_num_tokens / token_capacity is re-profiled from free memory at every start (WIN-SGL measured the same drift). It is reported with its delta and excluded from the restore gate; all nine configuration keys matched exactly.
assumptions.capacity_difference_vs_lru: the variant's pool came up at 1480094 vs M4's 1620892 for the lru run (-8.69%). The card requires the pressure target to use the variant's OWN capacity, so the comparison is pressure-normalised by construction: both runs stop at ~1.5x their own pool, which puts the bands at the same relative positions (the centre shifts by 12 document positions, far less than the ~259-document span and irrelevant to a ~30-document resident window). Absolute cached-token comparisons are additionally reported as a fraction of each run's own capacity. The cause of the capacity difference is NOT attributed -- it may be slru memory accounting or free-memory noise from the concurrently running gx10-qwen9b.
assumptions.launcher_health_recheck: launch_variant.wait_health reported 'container absent' at 40.4 s, which was a transient `docker inspect` failure over ssh while the container was in fact loading (docker events show create+start and no die/destroy; the container was Up throughout and reached health 200 at 07:50:18Z). The launch record keeps both the original verdict and the recheck, and no second launch was spent.
assumptions.corpus_reuse: documents are M4's cells/M4/corpus.jsonl verbatim (byte-identical prompt_sha256, same 4-word per-doc salts, same offline sizing); measured prompt_tokens 8514-8703 match M4's 8514-8703 range, so the two runs are paired, not merely similar.
assumptions.protocol_scope: phase D (append-note discipline) was NOT repeated -- M4 already answered it (note_unusable) and it is not part of this unit's one question; phase B (boundary probe) was not repeated either, which is why the resident window is only bracketed to [10,125].
assumptions.budget: 289 of 600 live requests, 1 variant launch, 1 restore launch, ~19 min wall clock; no extra config was attempted, so page_size x eviction-policy interaction and LFU remain untested.
